hints.junior: A slow retry set isSubmitting back to true without clearing hasError — the screen showed a spinner and a red error banner stacked on top of each other.
hints.mid: Three independent booleans describe eight combinations, but the render logic only ever meant to handle about four of them.
hints.staff: Boolean explosion: n independent flags describe 2^n combinations, and most aren't edge cases to handle — they're states that shouldn't exist at all.

hints.junior: Click Submit, then Server error, then Success, in that order, in each mode — watch what stacks up in broken mode.
hints.mid: Broken mode's badges show all three flags live — watch more than one go true at once. Fixed mode disables anything that isn't a valid transition.
hints.staff: The fixed mode's entire guarantee comes from a four-line transition table plus a render function that only ever reads one state variable — no extra runtime validation needed.

hints.junior: One variable holding exactly one named state — idle, submitting, success, error — can't be two of those at once, because it's just one string.
hints.mid: A transition table says which moves are even allowed from each state — an event that isn't valid from the current state simply doesn't fire.
hints.staff: A state value alone stops accidental combinations; a state machine's transition table also stops accidental transitions, and libraries like XState can statically check it for dead ends.

hints.junior: Writing the transition table down forces you to decide what can happen from each state, and just as importantly, what deliberately can't.
hints.mid: A hand-rolled switch on one state string covers most simple wizards — reach for a library once you need parallel or hierarchical states.
hints.staff: Don't let implementation booleans leak back in beside the state value — model anything state-dependent as part of that state, not as a sibling variable with its own lifecycle.

sections.junior: Hey! Today's case is about a signup wizard that once showed a loading spinner and an error message on screen at the exact same time.
The fix is using one named state instead of several separate true or false flags, plus a fixed list of which moves between states are even allowed.
Try to trigger submit, error, and success back to back in both modes, and see what the broken version lets happen that the fixed one simply won't.
Scattered booleans let impossible combinations happen by accident. One explicit state with a real transition table makes them impossible on purpose.
